naturalFeature.note: State GIS #139 and #140 are different waterfalls. Upper field point differs from GIS; avoid routing by ambiguous map pins.

publicLand.note: Visit Keweenaw identifies the lower falls as state land; regional reporting credits DNR and The Nature Conservancy with a published alternate public approach. This does not establish every intervening parcel or current gate.

seasonalArrival.note: 2026–27 Keweenaw visitor guide directs via Mandan Road to Fish Cove, while the 2023 visitor article identifies a rustic parking area. A 2024 DNR/TNC-reported alternative uses Hoar Lake Loop then leaves the vehicle before a berm. These are distinct descriptions, not verified interchangeable parking coordinates.

walkingCorridor.note: Visit Keweenaw describes about one mile on an unmarked rocky shoreline track from Fish Cove to Lower Montreal. Regional 2024 coverage describes a 1.3 mile unnamed-road walk on a separate approach. Neither is a current signed/maintained route or a measured route to Upper Montreal.

currentConditions.note: November 2026 public road/parking/gate and continuous foot-corridor verification was not established. Trailforks itself marks the historical Smiths-Fisheries approach as restricted, and its listed trailhead is not legal parking. DNR July 22 2026 trail map identifies a proposal/approval corridor, not a finished parking-to-falls route; no winter opening, GPS parking or safe shoreline passage can be asserted.

newConstruction.note: New finding: Copper Harbor Trails Club homepage says the Montreal Corridor is complete and announces a June 26 2027 celebration. However, CHTC's detailed KPT project story describes access to both falls in future tense, Michigan DNR's project page still describes 2026 construction, its July 2026 map marks RTPD approval rather than as-built walking connections, and CHTC's trail-status page does not give a dated Montreal-falls trailhead/parking opening. KORC's separate west-bank parking/connector remains permit-pending in its own 2026 notice. A complete long-distance corridor is not proof of a visitor-ready route or exact parking to either fall.

authoritativeEvidence.finding: DNR map labels North and South Mandan, Hoar Lake Road and Fish Cove and separately symbolizes State Forest Road, Other County Road, Private Road, ORV Route, and Snowmobile Trail. Dated general management planning map; not a current vehicle permission/lot or continuous named legal route.

Official Keweenaw PDF maps DNR forest roads open/closed to ORVs, restricted routes and non-DNR roads. Not a legal access or winter passability inventory for all county/private segments or any individual Fish Cove lot.

DNR state forest roads are DNR-managed roads open to conventional vehicles; trails and county highways are different categories. A DNR open-road legend cannot authorize every connecting non-DNR road, ORV route, or gated private drive.

State has easements over parts of Mandan Road; Fish Cove parking built with Keweenaw ATV Club. Identifies partial, not fully continuous, route rights. Entry year 2027 is the timber inventory planning cycle, not a road permit start date.

The current October 2026 road change proposals include conventional-vehicle open/closed status changes, but require 2027 director approval and are planned to take effect April 1, 2027; they cannot be presented as currently in force.

KORC says portions of Mandan Road were gated for hunters. Does not identify whether the gated portions intersect the separately published Fish Cove route. Do not infer specific gate position or whole-route closure.

Commission maintains county and trunkline roads under contract. Public roster and general winter notice are not a county-certified segment-by-segment Mandan/Hoar Lake status or construction/maintenance guarantee.

Published directions via Mandan and Fish Cove to rustic lot and unmaintained rocky shoreline to Lower Montreal; does not certify actual 2026 road jurisdiction, parking permission, maintained path, or current open winter arrival.
